_comment: JSON Schema describing the structure of brand_inputs.json produced by asset_ingestion.py. The chat workflow reads this schema to understand what's available.
title: Brand Inputs

total_words.description: Aggregate word count across all assets

asset_count_by_category.description: Asset counts per category (interviews, web, social, customer, prior_brand, competitive)

category.description: Source category — determines how the chat workflow weights the asset

format.description: Source format. Audio sources (Whisper transcripts) are flagged so voice-extractor can weight them appropriately for spoken vs. written voice.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 truncated to 16 chars — used to detect re-ingestion of unchanged files

metadata.description: Format-specific metadata (page count for PDFs, language for audio, columns for CSVs, etc.)

_category_weights_for_chat_workflow._comment: Reference for how the chat skills should weight different categories. Not enforced by schema, but documented here for skill calibration.

interviews.rationale: Founder/exec interviews carry the most authentic voice signal. They reveal what the brand IS, not what marketing wants it to be.

customer.rationale: Customer testimonials, support transcripts, and reviews are the primary persona evidence base. Real customer language beats invented personas every time.

web.rationale: Web copy reveals the brand's current public positioning. Heavily weighted for audit (what is the brand currently signaling?) but less for voice (often committee-edited and AI-templated).

social.rationale: Social posts (especially founder LinkedIn) carry stronger voice signal than web copy because they're typically less filtered.

prior_brand.rationale: Prior brand books reveal stated intent. The audit compares stated intent (this category) against demonstrated reality (web/social) — the gap is usually the most actionable insight.

competitive.rationale: Competitive material is reference for category convention analysis only. Never weight competitor voice in your voice extraction — that's how brands accidentally start sounding like their competitors.
